questions.enonce_markdown:
A discrete random variable $Y$ follows a binomial distribution with mean $1$ and variance $0.8$. Find, correct to 4 decimal places,

(i) $P(Y = 2)$

(ii) $P(Y < 2)$

(iii) $P(Y \ge 1)$

*[9 marks]*

The marks $X$ in an examination are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $8$. Find the value of $\mu$ to the nearest whole number, given that the probability that a candidate scores a mark more than $30$ is $0.1038$. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$X \sim N(\mu, 8^2)$ and $P(X > 30) = 0.1038$. Standardise with $Z = \dfrac{X-\mu}{8}\sim N(0,1)$:

$$P\!\left(Z > \frac{30-\mu}{8}\right) = 0.1038\ \Longrightarrow\ \Phi\!\left(\frac{30-\mu}{8}\right) = 1 - 0.1038 = 0.8962.$$

From the normal distribution tables, $\Phi(1.26) = 0.8962$, so

$$\frac{30-\mu}{8} = 1.26\ \Longrightarrow\ 30 - \mu = 10.08\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu = 19.92 \approx 20.$$

Hence $\mu = 20$ (to the nearest whole number).

(Check: with $\mu = 20$, $P(X>30) = P(Z>1.25) = 0.1056$, and with $\mu = 19.92$ exactly $P(X>30) = 0.1038$.)
